_doc.purpose: Recognition rows that ARE in the DB (auto-accepted at match time) but are demonstrably WRONG. The exporter drops these from the published badges. This is separate from data/processed/recognition_review.json, which holds matches that were never accepted and still await a human ruling.
_doc.why_a_config: src/build_db.py destroys and recreates the DB on every refresh, so recognition.id values are NOT stable across runs. Suppression is therefore keyed on (slug, source, matched_name), which is stable.
_doc.review_status: PROPOSED by the dashboard build on 2026-08-01, pending the owner's ruling. Each entry states the mechanism, not just the conclusion. Setting `active: false` restores the badges without touching code.
_doc.root_cause: HISTORIC. norm_name() in src/enrich_recognition.py used to strip venue types (bar, cafe, brasserie, trattoria...) before comparing, so two different restaurants could collapse onto one string -- or onto the EMPTY string -- and still score 0.9 with notes ' [exact name]'. Fixed 2026-08-05: venue types no longer strip, an empty normalisation falls back to the unstripped name, and check_norm_name() asserts both directions on every run. The entries retired that day are kept as the record. What remains is the case normalisation can never fix: a genuine namesake, where two different restaurants really do share a name.

suppress.reason: norm_name() strips the stopwords 'osteria', 'brooklyn' AND 'brasserie', so both 'Osteria Brooklyn' and 'Brasserie' normalise to the EMPTY STRING. osteria-brooklyn is the only one of the 648 participants that normalises to '', so it absorbed all 8 James Beard awards belonging to the Seagram Building's Brasserie (winner, 2000). None of these awards belong to Osteria Brooklyn. Fixed at source: norm_name no longer strips venue types, so this row is never produced. Kept inactive as the record of why, and enrich_recognition.check_norm_name() now fails the run if the collapse ever returns.

norm_name() strips both 'bar' and 'cafe', collapsing 'Bar Boulud' and 'Cafe Boulud' onto 'boulud'. These two nominations (2009, 2014) belong to Bar Boulud, a different Dinex room. Cafe Boulud's own six James Beard rows (matched_name 'Cafe Boulud') are genuine and are NOT suppressed, nor is its Michelin 1 star. Fixed at source: norm_name no longer strips venue types, so this row is never produced. Kept inactive as the record of why, and enrich_recognition.check_norm_name() now fails the run if the collapse ever returns.

Namesake, not the same restaurant. The 2011/2012 awards belong to Jesse Schenker's Recette, a New American restaurant at 328 W 12th St in the West Village that closed around 2015. The participant here is a French bistro at 103 Havemeyer St in Williamsburg; recettebrooklyn.com describes a French restaurant and never mentions Schenker or the awards. JBF's own records put both awards in Manhattan, which is what surfaced it.
